title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Make a Valid Array
summary: Given an integer array nums, determine the least number of adjacent swaps needed to place the largest element at the end and the smallest element at the start, ensuring the array meets the specified conditions.
statement: Given an integer array nums, determine the least number of adjacent swaps needed to place the largest element at the end and the smallest element at the start, ensuring the array meets the specified conditions.
constraints: A valid array has a minimum value at index zero and a maximum value at the final index.
When values repeat, choose occurrences minimizing the number of swaps.
hints: Use the leftmost minimum because it is closest to index zero.
Use the rightmost maximum because it is closest to the final index.
Add their distances, subtracting one when the minimum starts after the maximum because their moves cross once.
Any solution must cover both endpoint distances; these occurrence choices minimize them and only the shared crossing can reduce the sum.
editorial: Any solution must cover both endpoint distances; these occurrence choices minimize them and only the shared crossing can reduce the sum.

tests.explanation: Move the last value one leftward five places; the rightmost maximum then needs one fewer net move, totaling six.
The single value is both minimum and maximum, so no swap is required.
